key_insight: Different flow-matching paths can produce the same objective but very different SGD variance and convergence speed, so path choice is an optimization lever, not just a modeling detail.
engineering_relevance: For practitioners training flow-matching generative models, selecting or learning a lower-variance path can reduce training cost and improve convergence without changing the target FM problem.
method: Analyze SGD gradient variance as a function of the FM path.
Derive an optimal linear path for 1D Gaussian data under a linear velocity model.
Formulate PathOpt_θ with the constraint g_t ∈ G(p_t, v*_t) and give a sample-estimable equivalent formulation.
evidence_signal: The paper reports theoretical bounds plus experiments on Gaussian data, Gaussian mixture models, and real datasets to validate the variance-reduction effect.
watch_item: Variance reduction must respect the constraint of preserving the same marginal distributions and velocity field; unconstrained path changes can look better locally but slow overall convergence.
paper_title: Same Flow, Different Paths: Variance Reduction in Flow Matching
